Name: Hand-Drawn Sketch
Keywords: hand-drawn; sketch; whiteboard; excalidraw; roughjs; doodle; informal; brainstorm
Stroke Treatment: wobbly hand-jittered strokes; roughness 1-2 on rough.js scale; multiple overlapping passes per line
Fill Treatment: hachure and cross-hatch fills; low-density diagonal line fill instead of solid
Palette Mood: warm; informal; whiteboard-marker colors; muted pastel fills with dark ink outlines
Typography: Excalifont or Caveat/Gochi Hand for labels; handwritten feel
Background: off-white paper texture (#fdfaf3); faint grain; no grid
Node Rendering: rounded rectangles drawn with jittered path points; double-stroke outline for emphasis
Connector Rendering: single wobbly bezier line with hand-drawn arrowhead; slight overshoot at endpoints
Best For: brainstorming sessions; early-stage architecture docs; workshop collab boards; informal proposals
Do Not Use For: formal client-facing deliverables; print-ready technical specs; high-density diagrams over 40 nodes
Accessibility Notes: jittered strokes stay high-contrast against paper background; labels remain real text never baked into the path; roughness must not obscure text legibility
CSS Techniques: feTurbulence + feDisplacementMap SVG filter as css-only fallback when roughjs is unavailable; approximates jitter without JS

Name: Flat Minimal
Keywords: flat; minimal; clean; stripe-style; vercel-style; saas; modern; whitespace
Stroke Treatment: thin 1.5-2px solid strokes; no roughness; crisp geometric lines
Fill Treatment: flat solid fills; zero gradients; zero shadows
Palette Mood: restrained 2-3 brand accents plus neutral grays; generous whitespace reads calm and professional
Typography: Inter or Geist for all labels; medium weight for node names; regular for annotations
Background: plain white or #f8fafc; optional 20% opacity dot grid
Node Rendering: rounded rectangles with icon glyph plus label; consistent 8px corner radius
Connector Rendering: clean orthogonal or smooth bezier lines; solid stroke; simple arrowhead
Best For: public-facing architecture docs; SaaS product docs; investor decks; onboarding guides
Do Not Use For: dense low-level infra topology; playful or informal contexts; retro or nostalgic themes
Accessibility Notes: high contrast by default; pair accent color with icon shape, never color alone; label text at least 14px
CSS Techniques: CSS custom properties for token palette; box-shadow avoided entirely to stay flat

Name: Blueprint
Keywords: blueprint; schematic; technical; grid; engineering; cad; monospace; hardware
Stroke Treatment: rigid orthogonal lines only; no curves; uniform 1px hairline strokes
Fill Treatment: no fill or very light tinted fill; nodes read as outlined schematic symbols
Palette Mood: cyan/white lines on dark navy, or navy lines on white; formal, precise, cold
Typography: JetBrains Mono or IBM Plex Mono for all labels; uppercase node titles
Background: faint 1px grid lines at 10-20% opacity over dark navy (#0a1a2f) or paper white
Node Rendering: rectangular schematic symbols with hatched or cross-hatched fill accents; corner tick marks
Connector Rendering: strict orthogonal Manhattan-style routing; right-angle bends only; open arrowhead
Best For: hardware schematics; electrical and network diagrams; formal spec documents; RFC-style docs
Do Not Use For: casual brainstorms; consumer-facing marketing pages; playful storytelling flows
Accessibility Notes: high native contrast (cyan-on-navy); grid lines kept under 20% opacity so they never compete with strokes; monospace aids alignment for screen magnifiers
CSS Techniques: repeating-linear-gradient for grid background; stroke-dasharray for hatched fill accents

Name: Neon Dark
Keywords: neon; cyberpunk; dark-mode; glow; matrix; synthwave; devops; conference-demo
Stroke Treatment: thin bright strokes with outer glow; 2px core line plus blurred glow halo
Fill Treatment: near-black fill with translucent neon tint on active nodes
Palette Mood: cyan, magenta, lime on pure black (#000); high saturation, high contrast, futuristic
Typography: Orbitron or Space Mono for headers; JetBrains Mono for body labels
Background: pure black (#000) or near-black (#0a0a0f); optional subtle scanline texture
Node Rendering: dark panel with neon border glow; icon glyph rendered in accent neon color
Connector Rendering: glowing stroke with drop-shadow halo; animated pulse along active paths
Best For: conference demos; DevOps infra maps; dark-themed dashboards; tech marketing
Do Not Use For: print or paper deliverables; accessibility-first public docs; low-power mobile devices at scale
Accessibility Notes: glow filters must not reduce text contrast below 4.5:1; provide a reduced-motion static-glow fallback; avoid pure color-only status signaling
CSS Techniques: filter: drop-shadow for glow; text-shadow layering; prefers-reduced-motion swaps flicker for static glow

Name: Isometric 2.5D
Keywords: isometric; 2.5d; infra; cloud; 3d-block; devops; cloudcraft-style; depth
Stroke Treatment: clean 1.5px outline on each 3D face; consistent 30-degree edge angles
Fill Treatment: three-tone flat shading per block (top/left/right face) to fake depth; no gradients
Palette Mood: cool blues and grays for infra blocks; warm accent per service tier
Typography: Inter for labels; labels kept horizontal, never skewed with the block
Background: light neutral or dark slate; optional isometric dot grid
Node Rendering: extruded 3D block per component using CSS 3D transforms (rotateX/rotateY); stacked for depth
Connector Rendering: isometric-projected lines following the same 30-degree grid; arrowhead flattened to match perspective
Best For: cloud infrastructure topology; deployment diagrams; presentation slides
Do Not Use For: sequence or request-response flows; diagrams needing more than about 25 nodes; text-heavy specs
Accessibility Notes: 3D perspective must not be the only cue for hierarchy; keep labels horizontal and readable; face-shading contrast must meet AA against labels
CSS Techniques: CSS 3D transforms (transform-style: preserve-3d, rotateX/rotateY) built from flat SVG faces; no WebGL

Name: Glassmorphic
Keywords: glassmorphic; glass; frosted; blur; translucent; backdrop-filter; liquid-glass; premium
Stroke Treatment: thin translucent white border (1px, 20-30% opacity) outlining each panel
Fill Treatment: backdrop-filter blur with 10-30% opacity color tint; layered semi-transparent panes
Palette Mood: soft pastel tints over a vivid blurred background gradient; airy, premium, modern
Typography: Inter or SF-Pro-style sans-serif; medium weight for legibility over blur
Background: vivid gradient or blurred photo backdrop behind glass panels
Node Rendering: rounded glass card with backdrop-filter: blur(10px) and subtle inner highlight
Connector Rendering: soft translucent line with light glow; subtle drop-shadow for depth separation
Best For: premium product UI overlays; card-based architecture views; modal or overlay-style diagrams
Do Not Use For: low-power mobile targets; print output; diagrams needing crisp small text
Accessibility Notes: backdrop-filter blur can reduce text contrast; test On Color against the blurred backdrop, not just Fill; provide a solid-fill fallback for browsers lacking backdrop-filter support
CSS Techniques: backdrop-filter: blur(); layered rgba() panes; box-shadow for depth separation

Name: ASCII Terminal
Keywords: ascii; terminal; text-only; box-drawing; markdown; readme; cli-diagram; monospace
Stroke Treatment: unicode box-drawing characters form all lines; no vector strokes
Fill Treatment: no fill; interior is whitespace or repeated fill characters
Palette Mood: monochrome; single foreground color on terminal background; optional ANSI accent colors
Typography: monospace only (JetBrains Mono, IBM Plex Mono, or system terminal font); fixed-width grid alignment
Background: terminal black (#0c0c0c) or plain white markdown background
Node Rendering: box-drawn rectangle built from box-drawing characters wrapping the label text
Connector Rendering: box-drawing line and arrow characters routed on a fixed character grid
Best For: README docs; code comments; terminal UIs; lightweight version-controlled specs
Do Not Use For: visually rich presentations; diagrams needing color-coded roles; non-technical audiences
Accessibility Notes: perfect screen-reader support since content is real text; box-drawing characters need adequate line-height so glyphs do not visually merge
CSS Techniques: white-space: pre for fixed-width grid; text color transitions via opacity for tick/stream motion

Name: Pixel Retro
Keywords: pixel-art; retro; 8-bit; nostalgia; game-style; blocky; dithering; arcade
Stroke Treatment: no anti-aliasing; hard-edged 2-4px stepped outlines; image-rendering: pixelated
Fill Treatment: flat blocky fills from a limited 16-256 color palette; dithered gradients where shading is needed
Palette Mood: saturated primary colors reminiscent of 1980s-90s consoles; high-contrast blocky palette
Typography: pixel bitmap font (e.g. Press Start 2P); all-caps short labels
Background: solid dark or checkerboard pixel-grid background
Node Rendering: blocky sprite-style rectangle built from a fixed pixel grid; chunky 4x4 minimum block size
Connector Rendering: stepped stair-line connectors, no diagonals; pixel-grid-aligned
Best For: educational content; game-dev architecture; nostalgia-themed demos; indie community content
Do Not Use For: formal enterprise docs; dense diagrams needing fine text; accessibility-critical audiences
Accessibility Notes: small pixel fonts can fail minimum text size; provide a larger label overlay or tooltip; keep steps() animation timing predictable for motion-sensitive users
CSS Techniques: image-rendering: pixelated; animation-timing-function: steps() for chunky stepped motion

Name: Metro Map
Keywords: metro-map; transit; subway-style; routes; pipeline; data-flow-lines; network-topology
Stroke Treatment: thick uniform-width colored lines (route lines); rounded line joins at stops
Fill Treatment: solid color per route line; stops rendered as filled or ring-outline circles
Palette Mood: distinct saturated color per route/line for quick visual differentiation; light neutral background
Typography: Inter or Helvetica-style sans-serif; stop labels set perpendicular or alongside the line
Background: light neutral (#fafafa) or white; no grid; simplified non-geographic layout
Node Rendering: circular stop markers at line intersections and endpoints; interchange stops use larger ring markers
Connector Rendering: route line runs continuously through stops; 45/90-degree bends only, transit-map style simplification
Best For: data pipeline routes; bioinformatics workflows; network topology overviews; multi-path routing stories
Do Not Use For: precise geographic accuracy; single-linear sequence flows; dense component-level detail
Accessibility Notes: route color must be paired with a route label or legend, never color alone; interchange stops need a distinct shape, not just size
CSS Techniques: stroke-linejoin: round for line joins; stroke-dashoffset for travel-along-route motion

Name: Comic Storytelling
Keywords: comic; storytelling; narrative; speech-bubble; onboarding; user-journey; panels; illustrated
Stroke Treatment: bold 3-4px outlines with slight ink-brush variation on panel borders and speech bubbles
Fill Treatment: flat cel-shaded fills with occasional halftone dot pattern for shading
Palette Mood: bright, high-energy comic-book palette; bold primary colors with black ink outlines
Typography: comic lettering font (e.g. Bangers) for speech bubbles; clean sans-serif for technical labels
Background: sequential panel grid with white gutters between panels
Node Rendering: component drawn inside a speech-bubble or panel frame; tail points toward the acting node
Connector Rendering: bold directional arrow with motion-line flourish; panel-to-panel sequence implied left-to-right
Best For: onboarding walkthroughs; tutorial flows; user journey maps; non-technical stakeholder narratives
Do Not Use For: formal architecture review docs; dense multi-service topologies; enterprise compliance decks
Accessibility Notes: speech-bubble text must remain real selectable text, not baked into artwork; sequential panel order needs explicit reading-order via DOM order or aria-flowto
CSS Techniques: clip-path for speech-bubble tail shape; animation-delay-stagger to reveal panels in sequence

Name: HUD Monochrome
Stroke Treatment: 1px hairline in a single electric-cyan hue; soft outer glow reserved for the focused node
Fill Treatment: near-canvas glass panels; role is carried by label, shape and status chips, never by fill colour
Palette Mood: midnight navy + one electric cyan; amber is the single alarm exception
Typography: Inter for node labels; JetBrains Mono for edge labels, chips and data readouts
Background: deep navy (#0d1420) with a faint 44px line grid
Node Rendering: rounded glass cards with hairline cyan border; optional mono status chip in the top-right corner
Connector Rendering: thin cyan lines; async stays dashed, error switches to the amber alarm hue with long-short dash
Best For: cinematic walkthrough videos and beats mode; dark product/infra pages; mission-control aesthetics
Do Not Use For: print; light-mode documents; audiences who rely on role colour coding
Accessibility Notes: role is never colour-coded, so no colour legend exists; labels and chips carry role; amber is the only non-cyan hue and always pairs with a dash pattern

Name: Neubrutalism
Keywords: neubrutalism; brutalist; hard-shadow; acid; sticker; bold-border; playful; indie
Stroke Treatment: uniform 3px pure-black border on every shape; no tapering; no opacity variation
Fill Treatment: flat acid fills at full saturation; zero gradients; a hard 4px offset shadow in the same black as the border
Palette Mood: acid yellow, hot red, sky blue and mint on warm paper; loud, deliberately unsubtle, confident
Typography: Archivo Black or Inter 800 for node titles; JetBrains Mono for sub-labels; nothing lighter than 600
Background: warm paper (#fffdf5) with no grid; the shadows do the depth work
Node Rendering: square-cornered rectangle with a 3px black border and a solid 4px offset shadow; no radius anywhere
Connector Rendering: 3px black orthogonal lines with a solid triangular arrowhead; joins stay square
Best For: developer-tool product sites; indie product docs; workshop handouts; anything that should look built rather than designed
Do Not Use For: enterprise compliance decks; dense topologies over 15 nodes; contexts where the loud palette reads as unserious
Accessibility Notes: the black border carries the shape and the acid fill only tints it, so role never rests on colour alone; the offset shadow must stay the same black as the border or it reads as a second element
CSS Techniques: box-shadow with zero blur for the hard offset; rx:0 on every shape; no filter, no gradient

Name: E-Ink Paper
Keywords: e-ink; paper; print; monochrome; kindle; serif; grain; document; low-power
Stroke Treatment: 1px hairline ink; weight is the only emphasis axis, never colour
Fill Treatment: four flat grey levels standing in for what colour would carry elsewhere; a faint dither texture on the darkest level
Palette Mood: ink black on off-white paper; no hue at all, the way print has none
Typography: a serif (Source Serif / Georgia) for node titles, mono for data; print measure and generous leading
Background: off-white paper (#fdfbf7) with a faint grain overlay; no grid
Node Rendering: square-cornered rectangle, hairline border, grey level chosen by role; a mono role chip in the corner
Connector Rendering: hairline orthogonal lines; open arrowheads; async as a dashed run
Best For: print handouts; PDF specs; e-reader documentation; anywhere the diagram must survive a photocopier
Do Not Use For: motion-led explainers; diagrams whose story needs colour coding; conference-screen work
Accessibility Notes: no colour is used at all, so no colour legend exists and none is needed; role is carried by the label, the mono chip and the grey level, and every grey level clears 4.5:1 against the ink; motion is deliberately minimal because e-ink panels smear
CSS Techniques: repeating-radial-gradient for the grain; stroke-dasharray for the dither; transition-free state changes

Name: Bauhaus
Keywords: bauhaus; geometric; primary-colors; constructivist; modernist; poster; circle-square-triangle
Stroke Treatment: 2px black rule on every form; the line is structure, never decoration
Fill Treatment: flat primary red, blue and yellow plus black and off-white; each form takes exactly one flat colour
Palette Mood: the three primaries against black on off-white; disciplined, constructed, poster-like
Typography: a geometric sans (Futura-like: Jost, Poppins) in caps for titles; mono for data
Background: off-white (#f5f2eb) with an optional widely-spaced dot grid
Node Rendering: square-cornered rectangle in one flat primary, 2px black rule, hard 4px offset shadow; role marked by a small circle/square/triangle glyph
Connector Rendering: 2px black lines, right angles only, solid triangular heads; no curves anywhere
Best For: teaching posters; conference slides; editorial explainers; anything that benefits from looking composed
Do Not Use For: dense infrastructure maps; subtle brand contexts; diagrams needing more than three role colours
Accessibility Notes: only three hues exist, so roles beyond three share a colour and must be separated by the shape glyph and the label; the black rule keeps every form legible if colour is lost entirely
CSS Techniques: box-shadow with zero blur; clip-path for the triangle glyph; rx:0 throughout

Name: Claymorphism
Keywords: claymorphism; clay; puffy; soft-3d; pastel; rounded; friendly; toy; playful
Stroke Treatment: no visible border; the form is defined by a light rim highlight and a soft cast shadow
Fill Treatment: soft pastel fills with a paired inner highlight and inner shadow so each shape reads as moulded rather than drawn
Palette Mood: milky lavender ground with candy pastels; soft, friendly, low-contrast by nature so text must work harder
Typography: a rounded sans (Nunito, Quicksand) at 600+; mono only for data
Background: milky lavender (#f4f1fb); no grid, so the shadows read cleanly
Node Rendering: heavily rounded rectangle (24px+) with a light top-inner rim, a dark bottom-inner shadow and a wide soft drop shadow
Connector Rendering: thick soft-capped pastel lines with a faint shadow; rounded joins; blunt rounded arrowheads
Best For: onboarding material; product marketing; educational content for non-technical audiences; kids/consumer contexts
Do Not Use For: formal architecture reviews; dense diagrams (the shadows need breathing room); print output
Accessibility Notes: pastel fills sit close to the ground, so the on-colour must be a deep tint of the same hue rather than mid-grey; the shape has no border, meaning shadow contrast is the only edge cue and must not be softened further
CSS Techniques: layered inset box-shadow (light top + dark bottom) plus an outer drop-shadow; large border-radius; no gradient fills
